parsed.justification: (1) The replication explicitly states it was implemented from scratch using Mitiq + Qiskit Aer, with Aer NoiseModel depolarizing noise and Mitiq Richardson ZNE with unitary folding, so this satisfies “used real libs.” (2) The results qualitatively match the headline: under uncorrelated depolarizing noise ZNE strongly reduces bias (Exp1 bias_raw=-0.00650 to bias_zne≈+0.000094; Exp2 bias_raw=-0.1988 to bias_zne=-0.0269). Under time-correlated random-walk Z drift, ZNE becomes unreliable: Exp1 bias worsens (bias_raw=-0.00288 to bias_zne=+0.00531) and the scaled expectation values drop nonlinearly (0.0901→0.0646→0.0236), consistent with spectrum distortion; Exp2 shows large variance inflation under correlated noise (zne_std 0.0929 vs 0.00853 uncorrelated; variance ratio ≈10.9) and even overshoots above the physical noiseless value (zne_mean 1.016, with per-seed values up to 1.108). (3) Verdict PARTIAL because the qualitative degradation is clearly demonstrated (bias worsening/overshoot and major variance increase), but the “substantial residual bias” aspect is mixed in Exp2 (mean bias after ZNE is small and changes sign), and the correlated-noise model is a qualitative stand-in rather than the paper’s specific SchWARMA construction.
